subject: Best strategy to construct high density genetic map when phsical positions are avilable for only subset of total markers.

messages.author: e9ac8551453b903d
messages.subject: Best strategy to construct high density genetic map when phsical positions are avilable for only subset of total markers.
parts:
Dear Karl,
I am working with rice (diploid) RIL population and I am trying to construct high density genetic map with ~14000 SNPs. I have following queries

1)Of the total 14000 SNPs I have physical positions for ~10000 SNPs but dont have the physical positions for remaining 4000 SNPs. I want to use these 14000 markers together so as to identify genetic positions of 4000 SNPs (with unknown physical positions) realtive to 10000 SNPs (with known physical positions). What will be the best strategy to accomplish my goal. Is there any way I can use available physical positions with est.map function?

2) When I am trying to estimate RF many of my markers are showing RF > 0.5 (with high LOD) even though none of these markers switched (I have already eliminated distorted as well as duplicated markers) and therefore SNPs belonging physically to same chromosomes are getting split in to multiple LGs. What could be the possible cause behind this and how I should proceed with this.

I will appreciate any suggestions in this regard.

On Wed, Nov 14, 2018 at 7:02 AM Anurag Daware <avd.a...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Karl,
I am working with rice (diploid) RIL population and I am trying to construct high density genetic map with ~14000 SNPs. I have following queries

1)Of the total 14000 SNPs I have physical positions for ~10000 SNPs but dont have the physical positions for remaining 4000 SNPs. I want to use these 14000 markers together so as to identify genetic positions of 4000 SNPs (with unknown physical positions) realtive to  10000 SNPs (with known physical positions). What will be the best strategy to accomplish my goal. Is there any way I can use available physical positions with est.map function?
I don’t think R/qtl has good tools for this. I would look compare each of the 4000 markers to the other 10,000, and find position with fewest recombinants.

2) When I am trying to estimate RF many of my markers are showing RF > 0.5 (with high LOD) even though none of these markers switched (I have already eliminated distorted as well as duplicated markers) and therefore SNPs belonging physically to same chromosomes are getting split in to multiple LGs.  What could be the possible cause behind this and how I should proceed with this.

I can’t say without further information. For example, show the 2x2 table of counts of RILs with different two-locus genotypes for a pair of markers.

karl
